terms.name: Accessible description
terms.definition: Supplementary text announced after a control's name, carrying hint or error detail without becoming part of the name itself.

terms.name: Alpha compositing
terms.definition: The arithmetic that combines a translucent layer with what is beneath it, and the reason two stacked 50 percent layers do not add up to fully opaque.

terms.name: Art Nouveau
terms.definition: A turn of the century style of whiplash curves, botanical line ornament, muted jewel tones, and lettering drawn to fit the frame rather than set on a grid.

terms.name: Banner
terms.definition: A prominent message strip, usually spanning the top of a page or section, that stays visible until the user dismisses or resolves it.

terms.name: Breakpoint
terms.definition: A viewport width at which a layout is allowed to change shape, defined once so every screen in a system reflows at the same places.

terms.name: Card
terms.definition: A bounded surface holding a preview of one thing, usually an image, a title, some detail and one or two actions, that as a whole leads somewhere.

terms.name: Chat bubble
terms.definition: A rounded container for one message in a conversation, aligned and coloured by who sent it, often with a tail toward the sender's side.

terms.name: Color alias
terms.definition: A second name pointing at an existing scale so one palette can answer to several meanings, letting yellow serve as both warning and pending without duplication.

terms.name: Color wheel
terms.definition: A circular arrangement of hues that makes relationships between colours geometric, so a scheme becomes a shape drawn across the circle.

terms.name: Confirmshaming
terms.definition: Wording the decline option so that choosing it is an admission of something embarrassing, making refusal feel like a confession rather than a choice.

terms.name: Copy button
terms.definition: A small control beside a value that copies it to the clipboard and confirms by turning into a tick for a second or two.

terms.name: Dashboard grid
terms.definition: A grid of tiles, each holding one metric, chart or list, that a reader can often resize and rearrange.

terms.name: Device posture
terms.definition: The physical fold state of a foldable device, such as flat, book or tabletop, which a layout can respond to alongside plain size.

terms.name: Dock magnification
terms.definition: Scaling each item in a row by how close the pointer is to it, so the item under the cursor swells, its neighbours ramp down, and the row reads as bulging.

terms.name: Drop zone
terms.definition: The region that will accept a dragged item, usually highlighted while a compatible drag is in flight so the destination is unmistakable.

terms.name: Emergency exit button
terms.definition: A control that leaves the current page immediately for an unrelated site and tries to clear it from history, for readers who may be watched.

terms.name: Eyebrow
terms.definition: A short line of text above a heading that says what category or series the content belongs to.

terms.name: Fieldset
terms.definition: A group of related form controls sharing one question, with a legend that acts as the label for the whole group.

terms.name: Float animation
terms.definition: A slow continuous up and down drift on an idle element, so a static composition keeps breathing without asking for attention.

terms.name: Focusable disabled
terms.definition: A control styled as unavailable but left in the tab order with aria-disabled, so a reader can find it and learn why it is off.

terms.name: Frozen column
terms.definition: A table column held against the edge while the rest scrolls sideways, so the row's identifying value stays readable.

terms.name: Grabber
terms.definition: The short rounded bar drawn at the top of a bottom sheet to say the surface can be dragged.

terms.name: Haptic feedback
terms.definition: A brief physical vibration or tap produced by the device to confirm an interaction, mark a boundary, or signal success and failure.

terms.name: Home indicator
terms.definition: The thin bar at the bottom of a gesture driven phone screen, reserved space that app content must not sit beneath.

terms.name: Identicon
terms.definition: A generated default avatar derived deterministically from an identifier, so the same account always gets the same abstract pattern without uploading anything.

terms.name: Interaction color step
terms.definition: The convention that hover, active and selected are the next steps along the same scale rather than separate colours, so states are derived from one ramp.

terms.name: Kanban board
terms.definition: A row of vertical columns, each one a stage, holding cards that move sideways as work progresses.

terms.name: Language attribute
terms.definition: The declared language of a document or a passage inside it, which picks the voice, the pronunciation rules, and the hyphenation a reader gets.

terms.name: light-dark()
terms.definition: A CSS function that takes two colours and returns the one matching the page's current colour scheme, collapsing a theme's light and dark values into one declaration.

terms.name: Logical properties
terms.definition: Layout properties named by flow direction (inline start, block end) rather than by screen edge, so a layout mirrors itself in other writing modes.

terms.name: Material You
terms.definition: Google's personalization layer where the system derives an app's entire color scheme from the user's wallpaper, so every app shifts together.

terms.name: Microsurvey
terms.definition: A one or two question survey placed inside the product at the moment being asked about, answered in place rather than on a separate page.

terms.name: Monospace
terms.definition: A typeface in which every character occupies the same horizontal width, so characters stack into columns down the page.

terms.name: Named instance
terms.definition: A specific point in a variable font's design space that the designer has given a style name, so it can be picked like an ordinary weight.

terms.name: Nudge
terms.definition: Moving or changing a value by one small fixed step with an arrow key, with a modifier switching to a larger step.

terms.name: Optimistic UI
terms.definition: Showing the result of an action immediately and reconciling with the server afterward, instead of making the user wait for confirmation.

terms.name: Page curl
terms.definition: A page turn that lifts and bends the leaf away from the spine as the finger drags it, the most literal transition a reader can be given.

terms.name: Perceptual uniformity
terms.definition: The property of a colour space where equal numeric distances look like equal visual differences, which is what makes a generated ramp step evenly.

terms.name: Pop in
terms.definition: An entrance that scales slightly past full size before settling, so the element arrives with a small snap instead of simply being there.

terms.name: Privacy zuckering
terms.definition: Steering people into sharing more about themselves than they meant to, by making the permissive choice the easy one and the private choice several clicks deep.

terms.name: QR code
terms.definition: A square matrix barcode rendered in the interface to hand a link or credential to a phone camera.

terms.name: Reader mode
terms.definition: A browser view that throws away your layout and rebuilds the article as plain text the reader can restyle, which is a verdict on how readable the original was.

terms.name: Retro web design
terms.definition: A style that rebuilds the early desktop web on purpose: beveled window chrome, pixel and system type, garish color, and animated banners.

terms.name: Rule of thirds
terms.definition: Dividing a frame into nine equal cells with two lines each way and placing the important elements on the lines or their intersections.

terms.name: Scroll hijacking
terms.definition: Overriding the browser's scrolling so a wheel turn advances a scripted sequence instead of moving the page by the distance the reader asked for.

terms.name: Selection card
terms.definition: A radio or checkbox dressed as a card, where the whole tile is the target and the control itself is small or absent.

terms.name: Show more toggle
terms.definition: The control at the end of clamped text that expands it to full length and, when honest, collapses it again.

terms.name: Smart app banner
terms.definition: A strip pinned to the top of a mobile web page urging the reader to open or install the native app instead, with an install or open action.

terms.name: Spatial navigation
terms.definition: Moving focus by direction rather than by sequence, so arrow keys, a D-pad, or a TV remote jump to the nearest control up, down, left, or right.

terms.name: Stacking cards
terms.definition: A run of sections that each stick at the top of the viewport as the next one slides over it, so scrolling deals the page like a deck rather than passing it by.

terms.name: Stories
terms.definition: A sequence of full-screen cards that advance on a timer, paused by holding, skipped by tapping the edges, and gone after a fixed lifetime.

terms.name: Swipe actions
terms.definition: Buttons hidden behind a list row that a partial sideways swipe reveals, so destructive or common actions live under the item itself.

terms.name: Tag input
terms.definition: A field that turns each entry into a removable tag sitting inside the field, with the caret waiting after the last one.

terms.name: Time picker
terms.definition: A control for choosing a time of day, either as a dial you tap around or as hour and minute lists.

terms.name: Touch target
terms.definition: The area of a control that answers a press, padded out around whatever is drawn so a fingertip can hit it without catching its neighbours.

terms.name: Type specimen
terms.definition: A display of a typeface's characters, sizes, and styles made to show what the face can do rather than to communicate the text itself.

terms.name: Variation axis
terms.definition: One dimension a variable font can move along, named by a four-letter tag: lowercase for the five registered axes, uppercase for custom ones.

terms.name: Waveform
terms.definition: An audio track drawn as a row of amplitude bars, used both to show what is in the file and as the surface you scrub along.

terms.name: Yo-yo loop
terms.definition: A repeating animation that plays forward then backward instead of jumping back to the start, so a loop has no visible seam.
